study_identification_part.si4_title: Brain charts for the human lifespan

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Aggregate multi-study MRI data across the lifespan and fit normative centile trajectories (GAMLSS) to benchmark individual brain morphology and examine developmental milestones and clinical atypicality patterns.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset (ABCD; HCP; UK Biobank; AIBL; ADNI; and 100+ other studies)
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The abstract clearly states the dataset used.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Here we assemble an interactive open resource to benchmark brain morphology derived from any current or future sample of MRI data (http://www.brainchart.io/). With the goal of basing these reference charts on the largest and most inclusive dataset available, acknowledging limitations due to known biases of MRI studies relative to the diversity of the global population, we aggregated 123,984 MRI scans, across more than 100 primary studies, from 101,457 human participants between 115 days post-conception to 100 years of age.

rci4_hc_sex.reason: The total number of males and females in the healthy control group is not explicitly stated in a single sentence. However, the paper mentions sex-stratified analyses throughout.
rci4_hc_sex.supporting_text: Our decision to stratify the lifespan models by sex followed the analogous logic of sex-stratified anthropometric growth charts. Males have larger brain-tissue volumes than females in absolute terms (Supplementary Information 16), but this is not indicative of any difference in clinical or cognitive outcomes.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Study-specific (site-specific) random effects modeled for mean (μ) and variance (σ) parameters within GAMLSS framework; batch effects accounted for by study-level random intercepts; preprocessing pipeline included as fixed effect (five categories); compared to ComBat harmonization approach (Supplementary Information 5); validated through leave-one-study-out analyses
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: GAMLSS models were fitted... allowing for random effects on the mean and higher order moments of the outcome distributions... study-specific offsets (mean and variance) for each brain phenotype were also modelled as random effects... accounting for site- and study-specific batch effects... γ terms correspond to the study-level random effects
rci9_site_effect_handling.location: Bethlehem2021.pdf.md: Methods section, lines 417-418, 421, 443; Figure 1 caption, line 28; Bethlehem2021_sup.pdf.md: Section 5 on batch correction

nm2_modeling_method.answer: GAMLSS (Generalized Additive Models for Location, Scale and Shape)
nm2_modeling_method.reason: The paper clearly and repeatedly describes GAMLSS as the core modeling method. Extensive methodological details are provided including the use of generalized gamma distribution, fractional polynomials for age effects, and random effects for study-specific variation. This is the WHO-recommended framework for growth charts.
nm2_modeling_method.supporting_text: We created brain charts for the human lifespan using generalized additive models for location, scale and shape (GAMLSS), a robust and flexible framework for modelling non-linear growth trajectories recommended by the World Health Organization... For each component of the generalized gamma distribution, α terms correspond to fixed effects... β terms correspond to the fixed effects of age, modelled as fractional polynomial functions... γ terms correspond to the study-level random effects
nm2_modeling_method.location: Bethlehem2021.pdf.md: Results section, lines 37-38; Methods section, lines 440-443

nm4_response_variable.answer: Global cerebrum tissue volumes: total cortical grey matter volume (GMV), total white matter volume (WMV), total subcortical grey matter volume (sGMV), ventricular cerebrospinal fluid volume (ventricles/CSF); Extended global phenotypes: total cerebrum volume (TCV), mean cortical thickness, total surface area; Regional phenotypes: volume of 34 bilateral cortical regions (Desikan-Killiany parcellation)
nm4_response_variable.reason: The paper clearly describes all response variables modeled. The four main tissue volumes are the primary focus, with extended analyses on additional global metrics and regional volumes. Each is explicitly defined and illustrated in figures.
nm4_response_variable.supporting_text: GAMLSS models were fitted to structural MRI data from control subjects for the four main tissue volumes of the cerebrum (total cortical grey matter volume (GMV), total white matter volume (WMV), total subcortical grey matter volume (sGMV) and total ventricular cerebrospinal fluid volume (ventricles or CSF))... normative trajectories for additional MRI phenotypes including other morphometric properties at a global scale (mean cortical thickness and total surface area) and regional volume at each of 34 cortical areas
nm4_response_variable.location: Bethlehem2021.pdf.md: Results section, lines 45-46; Extended phenotypes, lines 64-66

nm5_predictor_variables.answer: Age (fractional polynomial); Sex (fixed effect, sex-stratified models); Study/Site (random effect); Preprocessing pipeline/software version (fixed effect, five categories)
nm5_predictor_variables.reason: The paper explicitly describes all predictors in the GAMLSS models. Age is modeled with fractional polynomials, sex as a fixed effect, study as random effects, and preprocessing pipeline as a categorical fixed effect. This is clearly stated in the methods and model specification sections.
nm5_predictor_variables.supporting_text: α terms correspond to fixed effects of the intercept, sex (female or male), and software version used for pre-processing (five categories); β terms correspond to the fixed effects of age, modelled as fractional polynomial functions with the number of terms reflecting the order of the fractional polynomials; and γ terms correspond to the study-level random effects
